outcome: Permanent contraception fulfillment by hospital discharge
cohort: Patients who delivered in 2018-2019 at three hospitals in Illinois, Ohio, and Alabama, and had permanent contraception as their contraceptive plan
finding: Patients with Medicaid insurance were less likely to have their desired permanent contraception fulfilled by hospital discharge compared to those with private insurance, especially among those who had unscheduled cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: The association between insurance type and permanent contraception fulfillment was stronger among those who had unscheduled cesarean deliveries (OR: 0.29; 95% CI: 0.12, 0.74) than those with scheduled cesarean deliveries (OR: 0.77; 95% CI: 0.32, 1.88).
